section_summary: This section concerns Japanese fishing and research vessels seeking access to American ports and Alaskan waters in 1936. State, Navy, Treasury, and other departments discuss courtesies, navigation hazards, customs rules, and the future treatment of ports that are not open to foreign vessels. The section also records Japanese crab-fishing activity in the Bering Sea and includes a 1935 memorandum on proposed California controls on Japanese-owned fishing vessels.

subfiles.title: Regulation of Fishing Vessels Owned by Japanese Nationals and Operating From American Ports
subfiles.about: Examines proposed state and federal controls on Japanese-owned fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: Dooman questions the California bill's legal basis, exaggerated supporting figures, and enforceability. He favors federal documentation requirements and naval control of strategically important Pacific Coast areas.

subfiles.title: Approval and navigation warning for Japanese cruises
subfiles.about: Approves both cruises while warning of hazards and restricted port status.
subfiles.summary: State warns that Bristol and Constantine Bays are risky and notes that several stops are not ports of entry, with Kiska a closed harbor. Approval creates no precedent.

subfiles.about: Promises fisheries officials' courtesies during Hakuyo Maru's visits.
subfiles.summary: Instructions will go to St. Paul Island and other relevant Alaska stations.

subfiles.about: Reports two vessels and twelve motor boats departing Hakodate for Bering Sea crab fishing.
subfiles.summary: One vessel will chiefly make fish meal; a despatch will follow.

subfiles.about: Confirms military commands were instructed to extend customary courtesies.
subfiles.summary: Instructions went to San Francisco and Honolulu commands.

subfiles.title: Treasury reply on Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.about: Authorizes customs collectors to assist Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Collectors at Juneau, Seattle, San Francisco, and Honolulu were notified.

subfiles.title: War Department reply on Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Explains War cannot provide courtesies in the Aleutians.
subfiles.summary: The islands are outside its jurisdiction; Ninth Corps Area was informed.

subfiles.title: Agriculture reply on Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.about: Promises regulatory assistance for Hakuyo Maru's visits.
subfiles.summary: Inspectors in San Francisco, Seattle, and Honolulu will facilitate the vessel's movements.

subfiles.title: Commerce reply on Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: States no objection to Hakuho Maru's proposed Aleutian calls.
subfiles.summary: Fisheries vessels, if present, will extend customary courtesies.

subfiles.title: Immigration Service reply on Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.about: Promises courtesies to Hakuyo Maru's personnel within immigration law.
subfiles.summary: Relevant Immigration Service officials have been instructed.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Immigration Service letter
subfiles.about: Repeats the promise of courtesies to Hakuyo Maru's personnel.
subfiles.summary: A poor copy of the preceding letter.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Japanese Embassy about Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.about: Records Kuroda's urgent inquiry about permission for Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Dooman says agencies are still being consulted and observes that the Embassy gave limited advance notice. He also recalls difficulties during the vessel's previous Alaskan visit.

subfiles.title: List of customs districts, headquarters, and ports of entry
subfiles.from: James H. Moyle, Commissioner of Customs
subfiles.to: Collectors of Customs and Others Concerned
subfiles.about: Publishes the current nationwide list of customs districts and ports of entry.
subfiles.summary: The list supplies the legal reference used to assess whether proposed Japanese vessel stops are ports of entry. It identifies Alaska's ports, including Juneau and Unalaska, and many districts elsewhere in the United States.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Alaskan and Mandated Islands port policy
subfiles.about: Records discussion with Commander Hill on reciprocal port access and future policy.
subfiles.summary: Hill conveys Admiral Standley's willingness to approve the current Alaskan visits while seeking Japanese access for American public vessels in the Mandated Islands. They discuss restricting future foreign visits to Alaskan ports after the Washington Naval Treaty expires.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Coast Guard watch
subfiles.about: Records Coast Guard inquiry about monitoring and assisting both Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Derby offers cooperation if State formally requests it.

subfiles.title: Dooman file note on Navy letter
subfiles.about: Flags questions raised by the attached Navy letter.
subfiles.summary: Dooman will return the papers promptly and make further suggestions.

subfiles.title: Navy assessment of Japanese vessel visits
subfiles.about: Assesses proposed visits against treaty rights, customs law, navigation hazards, and naval policy.
subfiles.summary: Navy lists stops that are not ports of entry, notes Kiska's closed status, and warns of hazards at Bristol and Constantine Bays. It raises concerns about unsupervised visits but does not object this year if approval creates no precedent. Navy recommends restricting future visits after January 1, 1937, and mentions a planned USS Alden cruise through Japanese Mandated Islands.

subfiles.title: Treasury reply on Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Authorizes customs courtesies for Hakuho Maru.
subfiles.summary: The Juneau collector will be instructed to assist during the Aleutian cruise.

subfiles.title: Protocol memorandum on Coast Guard notification
subfiles.about: Requests telephone notice of State's reply to the Japanese Ambassador.
subfiles.summary: Treasury wants the reply before telegraphing Coast Guard units about visits to possibly closed ports.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard courtesies for Hakuyo Maru
subfiles.about: Confirms Coast Guard patrol commands will assist Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: Bering Sea, Seattle, and San Francisco commands received instructions.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard courtesies and observation
subfiles.about: Reports instructions to assist and discreetly observe both Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Bering Sea patrol vessels will extend courtesies and watch their activities.

subfiles.title: Japanese acknowledgment of cruise approval
subfiles.about: Thanks State for approving the visits and warning of Aleutian navigation hazards.
subfiles.summary: Saito has telegraphed the warning to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Internal note on Japanese mother ships
subfiles.about: Summarizes reports on Japanese fishing vessels headed for the Bering Sea.
subfiles.summary: Toten Maru and Taihoku Maru reportedly will stay outside American waters; a newspaper separately mentions Tenyo Maru.

subfiles.title: Japanese crab fishing operations in Bering Sea
subfiles.about: Reports details of two Japanese mother ships' Bering Sea fishing operations.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a Foreign Office letter and identifies vessel tonnages and fish-meal production; the despatch continues beyond this section.
